method.label: 04 · Method
method.title: How I create value.
method.lead: Six steps. Each with something I did, not a nice phrase.

steps.name: Understand the problem
steps.text: Before building, I understand the context and the business. Talking to the people who use the software changes what gets prioritised.
steps.example: In-person day with clients in Buenos Aires (April 2026): demos, alignment and direct conversation about their real challenges.

steps.name: Align and negotiate priorities
steps.text: I agree on scope and priorities before writing code, and I hold the difficult conversations when they're needed.
steps.example: At Tsoft I take part in technical decisions with the team and support people who join.

steps.name: Design
steps.text: I design the interface and the system together: rules, states and limits before pretty screens.
steps.example: Volta and DentalOS: navigable demos with their own identity and labelled data.

steps.name: Build in stages
steps.text: I split the work into small batches, each with its acceptance criteria.
steps.example: Eclipse moves forward in documented batches, with approval gates.

steps.name: Show and validate
steps.text: I show something that works as early as possible and test it: automated tests, visual QA and demos.
steps.example: Velmar: a navigable demo for a client, with sample data.

steps.name: Deliver and learn
steps.text: I ship with CI/CD, document what I learned and apply it again.
steps.example: At Tsoft I work with deployment pipelines, integrations and CI/CD on Telefónica and Tuenti projects.

method.readsNote: Reading and learning, not certifications. I don't count them as practice until I have an example.

system.label: 05 · System
system.title: Not vibe coding. A system.
system.lead: I code with agents, but inside a process that plans, tests and delivers, with a person who approves.

points.title: Not a prompt: a system with roles
points.text: I built 11 agents with separate responsibilities (product, UX/UI, design, marketing, and frontend, backend, cybersecurity, games and trailer architects), with skills that load depending on the task.

points.title: Specification first, code second
points.text: Every change starts with a short document: problem, scope, acceptance criteria and how to roll back. The work is cut into small batches.

points.title: Every claim carries its level of evidence
points.text: I tell apart what I read, what I tested locally and what runs in a real environment. What I haven't tested is labelled «not tested».

points.title: Gates with human approval
points.text: The agents don't publish, spend or change prices on their own. I authorise publishing and spending.

points.title: Tested, not eyeballed
points.text: The main projects have automated tests, end-to-end tests with Playwright and CI that runs the tests and the build. Run of 10/27/2026, all green: Eclipse-Web 463 tests, Eclipse backend 779 and internal portal 132, plus 14 complete browser journeys.

points.title: Visual QA with binary criteria
points.text: Redesigns are compared against the previous state at several widths and with reduced motion. I state the limits: I test in Chromium.

points.title: Cost and honesty as design rules
points.text: No invented testimonials or clients, everything fictional says «Demo», and no new dependency or spending without my OK.

system.limits: What I don't say: that the agents work on their own, that the system has been audited or that a pentest has been done. The backend's database tests run in CI; I did not run them in the run above.

complia.title: CompliA
complia.summary: Conversational assistant for Telefónica's compliance portal. I designed and built it: RAG, validations, restrictions and recommendations.

sections.p: Telefónica's compliance portal digitalises internal processes, improves traceability and supports end-to-end flows: declarations, forms, interactions and administrative operations. I work on it as a Ssr AI Fullstack Developer at Tsoft.

list: Answers in natural language about historical and new compliance data (RAG on top of a language model).
Analyses sworn declarations and flags possible conflicts of interest and breaches of the programme's rules.
Helps issue rulings, assigns forms and builds the programme's reports.
States its limits: it can make mistakes and some processes need human action. A person confirms the ruling.

sections.p: I designed and built all of it: the RAG, the validations, the restrictions and the recommendations. The language model is one component; the rules that bound it are mine.
For confidentiality I don't show architecture, data, controls or internal screenshots from Telefónica or Tsoft. The video uses sample data.

handyx.title: HandyX
handyx.summary: Marketplace of home specialists in Mar del Plata. My own product.

sections.p: A person asks for a service for their home, specialists send quotes and the person compares the proposals.
I'm the only person on the project: product, design and development. HandyX is an independent product; it is not part of Eclipse.

list: In development; the launch is planned for November 10, 2026.
There are no results or metrics to show yet.

eclipse.title: Eclipse
eclipse.summary: My own development, AI and automation studio.

sections.p: Eclipse is my initiative to offer development, AI and automation. Its website shows demos of fictional businesses before proposing anything; everything fictional says «Demo».

list: A landing page with an industry selector and interactive demos.
A client portal in demo mode and its mode connected to the backend.
Its own backend, an internal portal and an email kit.
Automated tests and CI in the repositories.

sections.p: In batches with a specification, approval gates and QA, as I explain in «System».
Under construction. There are no clients or commercial results to show, and I don't invent them.

kinetic.title: Kinetic Studio
kinetic.summary: 32 motion-graphics trailers made with code: GSAP, canvas, WebGL and synthesised audio.

sections.p: A lab where each trailer is a page drawn live in the browser. The audio is synthesised too (WebAudio): there is no recorded music.

list: One paused master timeline per trailer: in the kit trailers, any frame can be frozen with ?t=.
Scores as data, synced with the image.
Particles in canvas and WebGL, text that turns into stars, simulations with a fixed seed.

sections.p: The «Meet Ignacio» trailer on this site uses the same ideas, with a new, smaller engine.
The kit is copied into every folder and has drifted apart. Unifying it is next.

tuenti.title: Tuenti
tuenti.summary: Gamification, top-ups and payments in Tuenti and Telefónica products, from Tsoft.

sections.p: Since 2024 I've worked at Tsoft on Tuenti and Telefónica products. First as a Jr Frontend Developer and, since 2026, as a Ssr AI Fullstack Developer.

list: Gamification: interactive and reward mechanics to improve engagement, such as the Tuenti roulette and the referral system.
Automatic top-up and a payments module.
In the Tuenti app: internal flows, backend logic, deployment pipelines and integrations.
Turning business requirements into technical solutions, alongside multidisciplinary teams.

sections.p: React, React Native, TypeScript, Next.js, Tailwind CSS, Node.js and SQL.
For confidentiality I don't show architecture, data, metrics or internal screenshots from Tuenti, Telefónica or Tsoft.
